paper.title: Distributed Learning Over Markovian Fading Channels for Stable Spectrum Access

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-user spectrum access over unknown restless Markovian channels with user-dependent rates (stable matching regret)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless Markovian arms (environment markovian) are out of scope from ontology v0.5.
unmapped: Each user-channel rate is an independent irreducible aperiodic finite-state Markov chain (restless) with unknown transitions
Rewards differ across users (heterogeneous multiplayer); regret measured against the unique stable matching w.r.t. expected rates
Channel states observed via carrier sensing regardless of collisions; users can signal interruptions and use opportunistic CSMA backoff to learn others' sample means
Algorithm requires constant L depending on Markov chain parameters (eigenvalue gap, x_max, r_max, pi_hat_max) and epsilon, I
settings.definition_quote: the rate of user $i$ on channel $k$, $r_{i,k}(t)$, is modeled as a discrete time, irreducible and aperiodic Markov chain on a finite-state space ... we define the regret ... as the loss in the expected aggregated data rate with respect to the stable matching solution that uses the true expected rates

bound.expression_latex: r(t) \leq A_{\max} (\sum_{i,k} (\lfloor \log_4(3A_{i,k}\log t+1)\rfloor+1)) + \sum_{i,k}[(4A_{i,k}\log t + 1 + M^{i,k}_{\max}(\ldots))(\mu_{i,S(i)}+\mu_{S^{-1}(k),k}-\mu_{i,k})] + M^2 A_{\max}(\ldots) + 2e\log(M+1)(\ldots)\sum_j\mu_{j,S(j)} + (A_{\max} + (M^2K+MK)\frac{6X_{\max}}{\pi_{\min}}\sum_j \mu_{j,S(j)})\lceil\log_4(\frac{3}{2}t+1)\rceil + O(1)

symbols.W: sum over users i and channels k of A_{i,k}*(mu_{i,S(i)} + mu_{S^{-1}(k),k} - mu_{i,k})
symbols.X_max: maximal cardinality of the Markov state spaces
symbols.pi_min: minimal stationary probability over all states, users, channels
symbols.R_S: sum_j mu_{j,S(j)}, expected total rate of the stable matching
symbols.N: number of users M in the paper

conditions: entries of the expected rate matrix U are all distinct (unique stable matching)
rate processes are irreducible aperiodic finite-state Markov chains, independent across users/channels
tuning: exploration DE epochs of length 4^n, exploitation epochs of length 2*4^(n-1)
condition T^(O)_{i,k}(t) > max{hat D_{i,k}(t), 2/I} log t with I = 7 eps^2/(48 (r_max+2)^2 L)

source.label: th:regret
source.quote: Assume that the proposed DSSL algorithm is implemented and that the assumptions on the system model described in Section \ref{sec:problem} hold. Then, the regret at time $t$ is upper bounded by: r(t) \leq A_{\max} \cdot (\sum_{i=1}^{M} \sum_{k=1}^{K} (\lfloor \log_4(3A_{i,k}\log(t)+1) \rfloor +1)) + \sum_{i}\sum_{k}[(4A_{i,k}\log(t)+1+M_{\max}^{i,k}(\ldots))(\mu_{i,S(i)}+\mu_{S^{-1}(k),k}-\mu_{i,k})] + ... + O(1), where A_{i,k} = max{2/I, D^{(max)}_{i,k}} if k in G_i, max{2/I, 4L/Delta_min^2} otherwise

results.notes: Exact finite-time bound simplified to its dominant log(T) terms (log log T terms in floor(log_4(3A log t+1)) and constants dropped, log_4 vs natural log absorbed into O). A_{i,k} depends on L, epsilon, gaps and Delta_min. Regret is relative to the stable matching via expected rates (weak regret for restless chains).

bound.regime: equal rates among users (varying among channels), K > M

symbols.N: number of users M in the paper

conditions: expected rates equal across users but vary among channels

source.label: th:regret
source.quote: under a common benchmark setting of equal rates among users (but still vary among channels), and $K>M$ ... In contrast, under DSSL, the regret scales as $O((\frac{1}{(\Delta_{\min})^2}+MK)\log(t))$

results.notes: Scaling claim stated in text following Theorem 1, not a separate formal statement; here Delta_min is the gap between the M-th and (M+1)-th best channels. Hard to reconcile with Theorem 1 where A_{i,k} appears for all M*K pairs.
